```
^\d{4}-(0[1-9]|1[0-2])-(0[1-9]|[12]\d|3[01])$
```

- `\d{4}` is the year.
- `(0[1-9]|1[0-2])` is the month, 01–12.
- `(0[1-9]|[12]\d|3[01])` is the day, 01–31.

This checks the format and the ranges for month and day. It doesn't check that the day exists in that month, so `2026-02-31` still matches. Leap years aren't handled either. Do that check with a date parser.

To find dates inside longer text, replace `^` and `$` with `\b`.
